items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear and there are section headers ("定价与优惠", "自动化测试接口"), but business code uses terse single-letter or cryptic names: `var o = findOrder(...)`, `f = findRefund`, `cv`, `q2`, `s`, `u` in getStats, and `fl.aftersale`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new 1548-line file, so this is capped at accept. Structure is good: pure priceLines/computeStats, ops.* shared by the UI and the API, and one delegated handlers map. The 68k-char omitted middle can't be checked for function length. The agent removed its self-test files before delivery.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are validated at boundaries: isInt qty checks, phone/address checks, an import validator, and a typeof check in importData. All 25 hidden tests pass. There are some magic numbers (MEMBER_PCT=95 is named, but rounding constants and 11-digit phone handling are inline). Error handling could not be fully checked in the elided code.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Confirmations exist for pay, ship, cancel (showing refund amount), restock, reset and import (confirmImport). The cart shows rules and coupon gaps, and invalid coupons are marked "已失效，未计入". Buttons are enabled by order status with an allowed-actions hint. The after-sale modal previews the refund, and toasts give plain-language errors.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The API calls the same run(ops.*), computeStats, queryOrders and importText as the UI. Money is kept in cents (toCents/toYuan, fmt(c)). Stats are recomputed from orders on every call. Import validates before overwriting; the agent's own test confirmed bad imports leave state unchanged.
